title: Environment retrospective
description: Retrospective on a coding session that proposes changes to the agent's ENVIRONMENT, not to the product: a deterministic pass reads the Claude Code transcript, the planning record and git history into friction signals (retro-signals) and an inventory of the checks already in place (retro-inventory); a fresh gsd-retro-analyst is worth running when the weighted signal sum reaches retro.signal_threshold, or when the schedule makes a retro due: once a milestone is planned and before its first phase runs (retro.at_milestone_start), and every retro.cadence_phases executed phases since the last retro (retro-cadence, journaled in .planning/retro/RUNS.json). Candidates are laid out by kind — mechanical → a check (project lint rule, hook, gate, verify_gates), judgement → reviewer skills (agent_skills.*), never CLAUDE.md, environment → settings — each tied to a signal and checked against the inventory. Nothing is applied automatically: the report is written to .planning/retro/ and a human routes each candidate. Accepted checks are journaled in .planning/retro/CHECKS.json so a check that never fires becomes a removal candidate. Claude Code only; every other runtime is degraded to git and .planning evidence and says so (ADR-5209).

retro.enabled.description: Enable the retro capability: the `gsd-tools retro` commands and /gsd-retro. Every read is local and read-only, and nothing a retro produces is applied without a human (ADR-5209), so it is on by default; set false to keep transcripts out of GSD entirely.

retro.auto.description: What the retro stage (`gsd-tools retro stage`, the same answer as `retro signals --decide`) answers at the end of a milestone's roadmap (roadmap:post), at the end of execute-phase (execute:post) and after ship (ship:post, friction only: `retro stage signals`) once a retro is worth proposing: the friction score reached retro.signal_threshold (trigger `signals`) or the schedule made one due (`milestone-start`, `cadence`). suggest prints one line proposing /gsd-retro; auto lets the caller spawn gsd-retro-analyst itself, and its candidates are still never applied; off always skips, the schedule included. When nothing fired the answer is skip in every mode.

retro.signal_threshold.description: Session friction score at or above which a retro is worth a model pass (score >= threshold). Each signal has units = count − min + 1; per kind the units are taken as a rate over the session volume (retro.volume_turns, retro.volume_calls), capped at retro.kind_cap and weighted — see src/retro-signals.cts for the weights. Calibrated on real sessions (ADR-5209): at 8 a retro is suggested for about one session in ten, almost all of them with explicit user pushback.

retro.cadence_phases.description: Executed phases of the current milestone since the last retro held in it at or above which a retro is due by schedule (trigger `cadence`), whatever the friction score. The retro stage checks it at execute:post, once per executed phase; ship:post does not repeat it. A phase counts once every plan has a summary. The default is 2: a retro every two executed phases. Absent means 2; 0 switches the cadence off. The count restarts at each retro (`retro prepare` journals it in .planning/retro/RUNS.json) and at each milestone; a journal that cannot be read pauses the schedule (reason `journal-invalid`) instead of counting from zero. `gsd-tools retro due` shows where it stands.

retro.at_milestone_start.description: Make a retro due once a milestone is planned: its ROADMAP has phases, none has started executing, it has not shipped, and no retro has been held in it yet (trigger `milestone-start`). The retro stage checks it at roadmap:post, the end of /gsd-new-milestone and /gsd-new-project; false removes that stage. A milestone boundary is where the environment is cheapest to change, before the phases that would pay for it.

retro.kind_cap.description: Units one signal kind can add to the score, at most — one cause (a broken hook firing on every call, say) never piles up a score on its own.

retro.volume_calls.description: Tool calls up to which tool-side signal units count as they are; past it they count as a rate per this many calls, so a long session is not a struggling one by length alone. Behavioural kinds use the main transcript's calls, environment kinds all calls including subagents.

retro.volume_turns.description: User turns up to which user corrections, interrupts and rejected tool calls count as they are; past it they count as a rate per this many turns.

retro.repeat_call_min.description: Identical tool calls with nothing edited in between before they count as a repeated-call signal (at least this many). Re-running a check after a fix is not a repetition, and polling tools (ListAgents, TaskOutput, ScheduleWakeup, …) never count.

retro.repeat_error_min.description: Occurrences of the same tool error before it counts as a repeated-tool-error signal.

retro.reread_min.description: Reads of the same range of one file with no edit to it and no compaction in between before they count as a reread signal.

retro.edit_churn_min.description: Edits of one file that rewrite lines an earlier edit of the same session wrote, before they count as an edit-churn signal. Successive edits of different places are not churn.

retro.nav_streak_min.description: Navigation calls (Read/Grep/Glob, read-only shell, structural MCP navigation) with nothing else in between before they count as a nav-streak signal. Any other call — an edit, a command, a spawned agent — or a user turn ends the streak.

retro.checker_loop_min.description: Plan-checker spawns in one session before they count as a plan-checker revision loop.

retro.checkpoint_min.description: Checkpoints reached in one session before they count as a repeated-checkpoint signal.

retro.hook_block_min.description: Blocks by the same hook before they count as a hook-block signal.

retro.excerpt_window.description: Transcript events on either side of a signal that the analyst is shown instead of the transcript.

retro.max_signals.description: Signals listed in a report; the rest are enumerated by id in `omitted`, never dropped silently. Caps the list, never the score.

retro.excerpt_chars.description: Maximum length of a redacted excerpt that leaves the transcript reader.

retro.check_stale_days.description: A check journaled in .planning/retro/CHECKS.json that has not fired in the transcripts of this many days (and was accepted at least this long ago) is offered as a removal candidate. Removal, like acceptance, is a human decision.
